title: THE HOLY WATER
note: Draft from the owner's Hebrew treatment (8.11.2026), fact-checked; see the script document for every correction. Panels are still to be drawn.

beats.say: A water bottle. Green. Handed over in the middle of a World Cup match. For fourteen years it was a rumour. Then Diego Maradona laughed on television.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Turin, the twenty-fourth of June, nineteen ninety. Round of sixteen: Argentina against Brazil.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Brazil came as favourites, and they controlled the night. Argentina, the holders, held on.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Before half-time, the game stops: an Argentina player is treated on the pitch. The physio, Miguel Di Lorenzo — known as Galíndez — brings the bottles.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Players from both sides drink. Brazil's left-back, Branco, takes a bottle too.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Branco said afterwards that he felt dizzy for the rest of the match. He said it the next day, and nobody believed him.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: In the eighty-first minute, Maradona runs at Brazil's defence and slides the ball to Claudio Caniggia. Caniggia rounds the keeper. One-nil.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Brazil are out of the World Cup.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: December two thousand and four. On Argentine television, Maradona says, laughing, that "someone" put a sleeping pill in the water — and that Branco was left completely dazed.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Argentina's José Basualdo later said the story was true. Coach Carlos Bilardo and Galíndez have always called it a myth.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

beats.say: Nothing was ever proven. But in Argentina it has a name: the holy water. File stays open.
beats.camera: One move per beat; hold for the line; the stamp and the score land on the word.

A player is treated, the Argentina physio hands out bottles, and Branco drinks. He says he felt dizzy. Argentina win 1-0. Years later Maradona laughs about it on TV. Full file on FanLife.
